diagnosis.hypothesis: Fixed swapped HTB class rates on wan1's WAN uplink (eth2). The business traffic class 1:10 (matching user1's 10.10.10.0/24 prefix) had rate 2Mbit instead of 8Mbit, while best-effort class 1:20 had 8Mbit instead of 2Mbit. Changed class 1:10 to rate 8Mbit ceil 10Mbit and class 1:20 to rate 2Mbit ceil 10Mbit. Validation confirmed all lab connectivity (0% loss on 14 paths) and observed throughput of 7.649 Mbps under contention, exceeding the enforced 6.8 Mbps floor for the 8 Mbps guarantee.
diagnosis.reference: On the WAN edge wan1, on eth2, the bandwidth allocation of the classes is inverted: the assured class 10 (8 Mbit/s for user1 to external1) got the small share and the background class the large one.

arguments.name: eth2
arguments.reason: The business traffic class 1:10 (prio 1, classifier matches 10.10.10.0/24 which is user1) only has a rate of 2Mbit instead of the required 8Mbit. The rates are swapped: class 1:10 should be 8Mbit and class 1:20 should be 2Mbit.

commands: tc class change dev eth2 parent 1:1 classid 1:10 htb rate 8Mbit ceil 10Mbit prio 1
tc class change dev eth2 parent 1:1 classid 1:20 htb rate 2Mbit ceil 10Mbit prio 2
changes.reason: The business traffic class 1:10 (matching source 10.10.10.0/24, which is user1's prefix) has rate 2Mbit instead of 8Mbit. Rates are swapped between the two classes. Restoring: class 1:10 should get 8Mbit guarantee, class 1:20 should get 2Mbit.
rollback_commands: tc class change dev eth2 parent 1:1 classid 1:10 htb rate 2Mbit ceil 10Mbit prio 1
tc class change dev eth2 parent 1:1 classid 1:20 htb rate 8Mbit ceil 10Mbit prio 2

final_response.summary: Fixed swapped HTB class rates on wan1's WAN uplink (eth2). The business traffic class 1:10 (matching user1's 10.10.10.0/24 prefix) had rate 2Mbit instead of 8Mbit, while best-effort class 1:20 had 8Mbit instead of 2Mbit. Changed class 1:10 to rate 8Mbit ceil 10Mbit and class 1:20 to rate 2Mbit ceil 10Mbit. Validation confirmed all lab connectivity (0% loss on 14 paths) and observed throughput of 7.649 Mbps under contention, exceeding the enforced 6.8 Mbps floor for the 8 Mbps guarantee.
